across_options.issue: Weight hierarchy changes along with family. B makes the screen headings bold; C makes Jamie offered $38, You keep, $31.40 and Ship by Tuesday lighter than A/B while its action labels appear heavier. D2 changes families, but ledger A3 and constitution Article 6.1 keep the role weights fixed. The comparison therefore does not isolate D2 (Article 14.4).

The field texture is not held constant: the fine curved lines are more pronounced in B, especially at the right of the offer card, and softer in C. Texture is a separate open decision, ledger D5, rather than D2.
C changes the jacket photo rendering: fabric and floor details appear softer and slightly different from A/B. The product imagery is not an invariant in this typeface comparison.
The endpoint of annotation 3 moves farther inside the Accept button in C. In A/B it sits near the left edge; in C it sits beside the label. The annotation geometry changes independently of typeface.
